# My plan for this year

Alright, let me think about this. I've been doing this for 35 years now, so I know my fields pretty well. Let me go through it crop by crop.

## How I'm splitting up my 64 mu

I've got cotton as my main thing, like most folks in my village. I'll put about 40 mu in cotton — that's the western fields where the soil isn't so good for grain anyway. Then I'll do about 15 mu of wheat-maize double crop on the better ground near the house, and the stevia company contracted with me again so I'll do 9 mu of stevia like last year. That adds up to 64 mu.

## Cotton (40 mu)

This is my bread and butter. I plant around mid-late April, usually after the big wind passes. I use hybrid seed from the township shop — same one neighbor Wang uses, about 35 yuan a mu for seed. 

For fertilizer I put down about 2 bags of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind) per mu before planting, that's about 50 kg/mu. Then when the cotton starts flowering I topdress with urea, maybe 15 kg/mu. My son-in-law says I use too much but last year the neighbor who cut back got worse yield so I'll keep doing what works.

I'll irrigate twice — once before planting to wet the soil, then once more if July is dry. The well is metered so you don't want to waste it. Pesticide — cotton always needs spraying, bollworm and aphids, probably 4-5 sprays through the season. That's expensive but you can't skip it or you lose the crop.

Last year I got about 230 kg of lint per mu. I'm hoping for similar this year.

## Wheat (15 mu) — already in the ground since last October

The wheat is already growing. I planted in early October after the summer maize came off. Used saved seed from last year plus some new Jimai variety I bought. Put down compound fertilizer at planting, about 40 kg/mu.

Right now around April I need to topdress with urea at jointing — about 12-15 kg/mu. And I need to irrigate. Already did the winter watering, will do one at jointing and one at grain-filling. That's three waterings total, which is normal for us.

Hoping for 450 kg/mu. Got 430 last year, conditions look okay this spring.

## Summer maize (15 mu) — after wheat harvest in June

Soon as the combine finishes the wheat in early June, I've got maybe 5 days to get the maize in. No time for tillage — I'll direct-seed into the stubble with the neighbor's planter, pay him 15 yuan/mu for that.

Fertilizer at planting — compound stuff, about 40 kg/mu. Then topdress urea at the big-bell stage, maybe 15 kg/mu. If it rains good in July and August I won't need to irrigate much, maybe just once. Pesticide just for armyworm if I see it.

Expecting around 500 kg/mu. Corn prices have been okay.

## Stevia (9 mu)

The company provides the seedlings and tells us what fertilizer to use. I transplant in late April-early May. More labor-intensive than grain — lots of weeding, my wife and I do most of it. Harvest in September-October. The company comes and buys it at the contract price. Less risk than cotton since the price is set.

## Labor and money

My wife and I do most of the work. Eldest son works in Handan city so he just comes for harvest. Younger son still in school. I hire some help for cotton picking in fall, maybe 20 days of hired labor. Total input cost I'm figuring around 35,000 yuan for everything — fertilizer, seed, pesticide, irrigation fees, custom planting, hired labor.
